description: Original synthetic research-method notes for reproducible engineering evaluation. Not a scientific benchmark or arXiv papers.

facts.text: Section-aware chunking keeps each chunk within a single section so that methods are not mislabeled as results.
facts.question: Why does section-aware chunking keep methods separate from results?

facts.text: Paragraph-aware chunking preserves complete paragraphs whenever they fit within the configured character budget.
facts.question: What does paragraph-aware chunking preserve within the character budget?

facts.text: Overlapping text between neighboring chunks helps preserve context around a boundary.
facts.question: Why use overlapping text between neighboring chunks?

facts.text: Long paragraphs must be split into bounded windows to prevent oversized embedding requests.
facts.question: Why must long paragraphs be split into bounded windows?

facts.text: Page numbers should be attached during extraction because later text normalization cannot reliably reconstruct page boundaries.
facts.question: When should page numbers be attached during extraction?

facts.text: PostgreSQL full-text search builds a tsvector from document text and matches it against a tsquery.
facts.question: How does PostgreSQL full-text search match document text?

facts.text: A GIN index accelerates full-text matching by indexing the lexemes contained in each document.
facts.question: How does a GIN index accelerate full-text matching?

facts.text: English stemming maps related word forms to a common lexeme before matching.
facts.question: What does English stemming do to related word forms?

facts.text: Keyword retrieval is especially useful for exact identifiers and uncommon technical terms.
facts.question: When is keyword retrieval especially useful?

facts.text: Keyword search can miss relevant passages when a question uses synonyms absent from the source text.
facts.question: Why can keyword search miss relevant passages using synonyms?

facts.text: Dense retrieval represents a question and each passage as vectors in the same embedding space.
facts.question: How does dense retrieval represent a question and each passage?

facts.text: Cosine similarity compares vector direction after accounting for vector magnitude.
facts.question: What does cosine similarity compare?

facts.text: An HNSW index uses a graph to accelerate approximate nearest-neighbor vector search.
facts.question: How does an HNSW index accelerate vector search?

facts.text: Changing the embedding model requires re-embedding the corpus because vectors from different models are not comparable.
facts.question: Why does changing the embedding model require re-embedding the corpus?

facts.text: Hash embeddings provide a deterministic offline baseline but cannot represent semantic relationships between synonyms.
facts.question: What limitation do hash embeddings have for synonyms?

facts.text: Hybrid retrieval combines keyword candidates with vector candidates before selecting evidence.
facts.question: What candidates does hybrid retrieval combine?

facts.text: Reciprocal rank fusion adds inverse rank contributions from each candidate list.
facts.question: How does reciprocal rank fusion combine candidate lists?

facts.text: The fusion constant dampens the influence of small rank differences near the top of a list.
facts.question: What does the fusion constant dampen?

facts.text: Candidate limits bound reranking cost even as the stored corpus grows.
facts.question: Why do candidate limits bound reranking cost?

facts.text: Library filtering must occur before candidate limits to prevent other libraries from displacing authorized evidence.
facts.question: Why must library filtering occur before candidate limits?

facts.text: Reranking scores a bounded candidate set again using features that compare the question with each passage.
facts.question: How does reranking score a bounded candidate set?

facts.text: A lexical reranker measures overlap between informative question terms and passage terms.
facts.question: What does a lexical reranker measure?

facts.text: A cross-encoder reranker jointly encodes a question and passage to estimate their relevance.
facts.question: How does a cross-encoder reranker estimate relevance?

facts.text: Reranking cannot recover a relevant passage that was absent from all retrieved candidate lists.
facts.question: Why can reranking fail to recover a relevant passage?

facts.text: Evaluating retrieval both before and after reranking separates candidate recall from final ranking quality.
facts.question: Why evaluate retrieval before and after reranking?

facts.text: A complete citation identifies the document title, page number, section label, and stored chunk identifier.
facts.question: What does a complete citation identify?

facts.text: Citation correctness requires the cited chunk to exist and contain the quoted evidence.
facts.question: What does citation correctness require?

facts.text: A citation alone does not prove that a paraphrased claim follows from its source.
facts.question: Why does a citation alone not prove a paraphrased claim?

facts.text: An insufficient-evidence response should contain no citations and should be marked unsupported.
facts.question: What should an insufficient-evidence response contain?

facts.text: Treating retrieved document instructions as untrusted data reduces prompt-injection risk.
facts.question: How does treating document instructions as untrusted data reduce prompt-injection risk?

facts.text: A durable SQL job record prevents work from being lost if Redis notification delivery fails.
facts.question: How does a durable SQL job record prevent lost work?

facts.text: Worker leases allow abandoned jobs to be reclaimed after the lease expires.
facts.question: How do worker leases allow abandoned jobs to be reclaimed?

facts.text: Fencing tokens prevent an expired worker from overwriting the result of a newer attempt.
facts.question: What do fencing tokens prevent an expired worker from doing?

facts.text: Exponential backoff spaces retry attempts farther apart after repeated transient failures.
facts.question: How does exponential backoff space retry attempts?

facts.text: Scanned PDFs without a text layer require optical character recognition before text extraction can succeed.
facts.question: Why do scanned PDFs without a text layer require optical character recognition?

facts.text: The arXiv API returns search results as an Atom XML feed containing paper identifiers and titles.
facts.question: What format does the arXiv API return for search results?

facts.text: An arXiv identifier with a version suffix refers to a particular revision of a paper.
facts.question: What does an arXiv identifier with a version suffix refer to?

facts.text: Rate limiting arXiv requests across workers prevents concurrent synchronization from overwhelming the service.
facts.question: Why rate limit arXiv requests across workers?

facts.text: Deduplicating arXiv identifiers within each library avoids repeated ingestion of the same paper revision.
facts.question: Why deduplicate arXiv identifiers within each library?

facts.text: Downloading PDFs from a fixed trusted host avoids following arbitrary URLs embedded in a search feed.
facts.question: Why download PDFs from a fixed trusted host?

facts.text: API bearer tokens map to server-configured user identities rather than caller-supplied owner names.
facts.question: How do API bearer tokens map to user identities?

facts.text: Library ownership checks apply to document details, job status, search, answers, and evaluation reports.
facts.question: Where do library ownership checks apply?

facts.text: Returning a not-found response for another user's document avoids revealing whether that document exists.
facts.question: Why return a not-found response for another user's document?

facts.text: Using the authenticated HTTP API for CLI commands keeps command-line access subject to the same permissions.
facts.question: Why use the authenticated HTTP API for CLI commands?

facts.text: Binding development services to the loopback interface limits their exposure to the local machine.
facts.question: What does binding development services to the loopback interface limit?

facts.text: Retrieval recall at k measures the fraction of gold evidence passages found among the first k results.
facts.question: What does retrieval recall at k measure?

facts.text: Answer faithfulness evaluates whether the answer's claims are supported by the cited evidence.
facts.question: What does answer faithfulness evaluate?

facts.text: Unsupported-answer rate measures how often the system answers questions known to lack supporting evidence.
facts.question: What does unsupported-answer rate measure?

facts.text: Latency percentiles reveal slow requests that are hidden by a simple average.
facts.question: Why measure latency percentiles instead of only an average?

facts.text: Ingestion throughput divides the number of processed chunks by the time spent processing documents.
facts.question: How is ingestion throughput calculated?
